correctness.rationale: Resident stationarity gives the exact weighted mean-zero potential ∫Qr=0; nonideal r is nonconstant and sign-changing. The self-adjoint Rayleigh quotient tested at w=1+εr gives strict positive principal eigenvalue at every finite diffusion. The Feynman–Hellmann derivative is strictly negative because a constant top eigenfunction would force r constant. Bump functions and the Neumann gap give endpoint limits. A simple-eigenvalue perturbation with the weighted-mean-zero Poisson corrector proves Λ(d)=C/d+O(d^{-2}). Uniform capacity loss shifts the spectrum exactly; monotonicity yields the unique cutoff. Exact rational cosine moments give the positive-capacity counterexample with bound 13/700 and C=1/32. The included independent arithmetic implementation was run successfully; infinite-dimensional statements rest on the written proof.

originality.rationale: The motivating primary article explicitly asks the equal-capacity nonideal-resident question but establishes the mimicking-invader result only with a nonnegative capacity advantage, strict somewhere. Its numerical lower-capacity examples have no all-mobility classification. Classical weighted variational eigenvalue methods and discrete-patch evolutionary-invasion theorems do not state the coupled strict positive eigenvalue, unique capacity-loss diffusion cutoff, asymptotic constant, and exact disadvantaged invasion witness proved here. Actual targeted mathematical-record searches found no covering claim; possible unindexed equivalences remain a risk.
residual_risks: Other unindexed diffusion-selection literature may formulate this as a corollary of a broader variational theorem.
The 2007 discrete-patch paper was accessible with some displayed equations incompletely rendered; however, its finite-patch hypotheses differ materially from the present continuous operator.

value.rationale: The primary paper raises this precise equal-capacity invasion question as open. Resolving it uniformly over finite movement rates and establishing a sharp tolerated resource-disadvantage curve explains when directed habitat tracking compensates for uniform reproductive loss, which is meaningful in spatial ecological competition. The exact positive-capacity witness and asymptotic d_c~C/c quantify a mathematically motivated management tradeoff. No larger nonlinear or stochastic assertion is inferred.
